title: streaming-lifecycle-controls: robust client-cancel, disconnect handling, reconnect/resume and server timeout coordination
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: Streaming endpoints need robust lifecycle controls to avoid wasted work, inconsistent billing, and client-visible glitches when users cancel, lose connectivity, or reconnect. This PR implements coordinated lifecycle handling across the gateway, runtime and openai-compat layer: (1) explicit client cancel semantics that surface immediately to the runtime and stop token generation work, (2) robust disconnect handling where transient network failures allow a short resume window before server-side cancellation, (3) reconnect/resume token handshake to continue streams without restarting from scratch when supported, and (4) server-side idle/receive timeouts that clean up orphaned streams while respecting resume windows. Design summary: - Introduces a per-stream lifecycle state machine (OPEN -> CLIENT_CANCELLED -> DISCONNECTED_WAIT -> RESUMED -> SERVER_CANCELLED/COMPLETED) encoded as a compact header and a runtime-safe token that the gateway and runtime can use to correlate reconnects. - Client cancel becomes an idempotent, first-class API signal ("x-rw-client-cancel: 1") for the OpenAI-compat layer and native streaming protocol. Cancel causes the gateway to send a short-circuit to the runtime; runtime flushes KV cache writes, emits a final CANCELLED event to tracing/metrics and immediately frees compute/batch slots. - Disconnect handling: on network disconnect we keep the stream state in DISCONNECTED_WAIT for a configurable resume_window (default 30s). During that window the runtime keeps KV cache and partial generation state pinned but deprioritized; compute is released for active streams but we retain enough state to resume cheaply. - Reconnect/resume: clients that reconnect send the resume token ("x-rw-resume-token: <token>") and optional last-seen token index. Gateway validates the token, maps it to in-memory stream state, and if within resume_window instructs runtime to resume generation from the last emitted token. If resume_window expired or token mismatch, gateway falls back to a full restart and annotates response with "x-rw-resume-failed" for client SDKs to handle. - Server timeouts: two timeouts coordinated between components: receive_timeout (how long gateway will wait for client activity before moving to DISCONNECTED_WAIT) and server_idle_timeout (how long runtime will keep pinned resume state before full eviction). Defaults chosen to balance cost and UX: receive_timeout=10s, resume_window=30s, server_idle_timeout=120s. Backwards compatibility: OpenAI-compat clients that don't send the new headers get current behavior (immediate cancellation on TCP close). The OpenAI-compat shim mirrors the same headers as X-RW-* but also supports the existing behavior depending on compatibility mode. Implementation notes: - Gateway: header handling, resume token generation (HMAC of stream id + expiry), in-memory index and metrics, and a small finite-state-machine to coordinate messages to the runtime. - Runtime: added lifecycle hooks to accept cancel/resume RPCs, checkpoint partial generation state (KV cache pointers + last token index) in memory-only ephemeral slots, and async eviction path that emits metrics and traces on full eviction. - SDKs: added opt-in resume support to the TS/python SDKs (separate PRs will surface examples). - Metrics/tracing: new metrics rw.streams.resume_attempts, rw.streams.resume_success, rw.streams.evictions and spans for lifecycle transitions. - Tests: unit tests for FSM transitions, e2e tests simulating client disconnect+reconnect, and a canary workload to assert cost/regressions. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (linked in PR) - [x] Gateway header + resume token implementation - [x] Runtime lifecycle hooks + eviction path - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Canary performance run - [x] Documentation snippets for OpenAI-compat behavior Rollout plan: feature behind gate (feature.streaming_resume) enabled for internal canary, then staged rollout to 10% hosted traffic, monitor resume_success metric and evictions, then gradual ramp. Related: ENG-2314 (streaming UX improvements), ENG-2298 (runtime batching state retention).

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Nice end-to-end. Two concerns: 1) resume token entropy - can we include a derivation salt tied to deployment? 2) eviction timing seems optimistic for high-memory models. Please add tests for resume_token replay attempts.
Aisha Khan: Addressed both - token now includes deployment salt and monotonic counter; added resume replay test and increased default server_idle_timeout to 120s. See commit 14b7f23.
Jordan Lee: Can we make the resume window configurable per-customer (Dedicated)? I think teams will want longer windows for mobile-heavy apps.
Aisha Khan: Added config hook and dedicated/default override in gateway config; documented in docs/streaming.md.
Priya Nair: LGT M on runtime changes but please ensure evictions emit structured events to S3 for compliance customers.
Aisha Khan: Added eviction event emitter and S3 sink toggle under compliance feature flag; refactored eviction path to async append-only emitter.

release_notes: Adds coordinated streaming lifecycle controls: client-cancel header, disconnect resume window, reconnect/resume token handshake, and server-side eviction/timeouts. Gate-controlled rollout and config knobs for Dedicated/private deployments.
notes_for_backport: No backport required for stable branch; for release branches, patch for gateway header parsing and runtime eviction should be applied together to avoid partial behavior.
